metadata.description: An explicit edge to dbx-cli:build-base, NOT `^build`. This entry point compiles into the parent's dist directory, which `dbx-cli:build-base` deletes and rewrites (rollup `deleteOutputPath: true`), so it cannot run before the parent -- but the edge has to be spelled out, because `^build` here would resolve to dbx-cli:build, which depends on this very target: a hard cycle. That XOR is the whole design constraint -- either the children get `^build` or the parent aggregates them, never both. Aggregating is the side that keeps one writer per dist directory.  It also imports the SIBLING entry point @dereekb/dbx-cli/validate (the notification extractor, rules and manifest builder), so it carries a sibling edge to dbx-cli-validate:build-base, which in turn orders that sibling's generate-rule-catalog (the bundled rule catalog) and its manifest-extract / model-test / util:build edges ahead of this bundle. A sibling edge is spelled as `build-base` (not `build`): siblings compile into this same dist directory and have no `build` of their own.  `skipTypeCheck` is true, the same choice as dbx-cli-validate and dbx-components-mcp: the @dereekb/dbx-cli/validate barrel this bundle imports carries existing type errors in unrelated clusters (ui-smell-check, storagefile-m-*, notification-m-validate-folder), so a type-checked bundle of it fails. The notification sources this generator uses are type-checked by hand with `tsc -p packages/dbx-cli/generate-notification-manifest/tsconfig.tool.json --noEmit` until those are fixed.
